item.title: Re: Consider this
item.content:encoded:
As the theme of it appears to be essentially "punishing the sin of greed", I would expect everyone would be OK. Maybe the generous soul would be given an extra hand or something weird. But probably so long as they were choosing to give it to you, no strings, and you either refused, or accepted gratefully, you'd be fine. If instead both parties took two candies each, and you then forcibly relieved the other subject of one or more of theirs ("taking" rather than "receiving"), you might find yourself facing the same fate as if you'd removed three or more from the bowl in the first place.

I sort of concur with various other comments… this feels like a half finished shell that was abandoned ten years ago and never really fleshed out properly.

Longer discussion, testing:

+ show block
– hide block

Like, there's no mention of whether the bowl refills, if so what rate it fills at and if it's possible to therefore empty it by having multiple subjects take two candies each… or if you have to add your own candy to start with (in which case once it's finally emptied you could just turn it upside down… maybe drop it into a steel smelting crucible and slag it…), whether you can add more on top of ones that self fill, even really what type they are, whether some added to the bowl stay the same or change to match, and if adding additional candy to the bowl allows you to then remove 2+however many you added or not, or if it even does something weird like giving you extra hands… or if the removed candies appear to have any anomalous effects or are, as far as anyone can tell, entirely mundane other than for the 1001 arabian nights approach to discouraging theft… etc.

Also, can the severed appendages be reattached? Is there any medical/surgical/psychological/memetic barrier to that? And given the experience of the amputee and the whole "resetting" feature, if the subject survives for the full 24 hours (if you've just suffered a double amputation with molecularly clean cuts - something which isn't particularly conducive to quick clotting even if we ignore the severing of major arteries - you're likely to rapidly bleed out without immediate medical response) and the hands are suitably preserved, do they magically reappear/reattach themselves?

All of which could probably be tackled without quite so much text, probably just three or four additional sentences hinting that additional testing was carried out beyond the "yep, it cuts your hands off no matter what, even if they're fake hands" bit, and particularly on the candies themselves.

Longer discussion, containment:

+ show block
– hide block

The Kondraki thing I can maybe understand if the idea is that he's a sword wielding (? might be getting my doctors mixed) grouch who doesn't have any kind of sweet tooth, and the object has some kind of marginal compulsive/memetic effect that draws people to it and eventually causes them to succumb to the temptation of taking a third candy, even if they know the consequences and it's locked up in an otherwise secure locker. Maybe it being in a floor safe under the desk in his office would be the safest place for it, under those circumstances.

But it does rather seem like a better procedure would be necessary. For example it being kept in a secure locker with a time lock (ie it can only open for a brief period at a certain time each day, even if you have the key), and the key being held at a different site sufficiently distant that you can't get back within the time taken to remove the bowl from storage, test it, and put it back (the locker remaining open for the duration and automatically locking only once closed with the bowl detected as being back inside), itself in a more regular locker that can only be opened using a key held by someone working at the site where 330 is stored, and there being a tertiary lock (time is primary, key is secondary) that only opens if said keyholder is autonomously confirmed as still being present at the remote site, having dispatched someone from that site to deliver it to open 330s locker. With all the usual layers of multi-party authorisation needed between multiple sites acting as a check. A bit of a longwinded explanation but I hope you see what I'm getting at - it would be difficult for any compulsion effect to therefore cause the keyholder to wait until no-one's looking and use the key to try and sneak some candy, possibly trying for three pieces.

…Of course if it's tested and confirmed as having no such effect it can just be chucked in a standard locker and left to rust.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
careful - the question "does anyone know what would happen if X" doesn't make sense in a Foundation context. The answer is always both 'yes' and 'no' - 'yes' because what would happen is whatever we want to happen, and 'no' because it's not real, it's all made up, none of it actually happens.

What you mean is "What would happen if X" - a phrasing which inspires flights of imagination.

That said, those are damn good questions. What do you think would be the most interesting result?
